landmarks.name: Taj Mahal
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site in Agra, built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, renowned for its white marble architecture.

landmarks.name: Red Fort
landmarks.writeup: Historic fort in Delhi that served as the main residence of Mughal emperors, symbolizing India's rich history and independence.

landmarks.name: Qutub Minar
landmarks.writeup: A 73-meter tall minaret in Delhi, built in the early 13th century, representing Indo-Islamic architecture.

landmarks.name: Gateway of India
landmarks.writeup: An iconic arch monument in Mumbai, built during the British Raj to commemorate the visit of King George V and Queen Mary.

landmarks.name: Hampi
landmarks.writeup: Ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire capital, known for its ancient temples and unique Dravidian architecture.

cultural_events.name: Diwali
cultural_events.writeup: The festival of lights celebrated across India symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and good over evil.

cultural_events.name: Holi
cultural_events.writeup: Known as the festival of colors, it marks the arrival of spring and celebrates love and the triumph of good.

cultural_events.name: Durga Puja
cultural_events.writeup: A major Hindu festival in eastern India honoring the goddess Durga with elaborate rituals and cultural performances.

cultural_events.name: Eid-ul-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A significant Islamic festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with prayers and feasting.

cultural_events.name: Pongal
cultural_events.writeup: A harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, thanking the Sun God for agricultural abundance.

food_writeup: Indian cuisine is diverse and characterized by the use of various spices, herbs, and regional ingredients. Popular dishes include biryani, dosa, samosas, butter chicken, and a wide variety of vegetarian and non-vegetarian options reflecting cultural and religious diversity.
brief_history: India has a rich history dating back to the Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2500 BCE). It was home to major empires such as the Maurya and Gupta Empires, followed by Islamic Sultanates and the Mughal Empire. Colonized by the British in the 18th century, India gained independence in 1947 and became a democratic republic.

important_people.name: Mahatma Gandhi
important_people.description: Leader of the Indian independence movement

important_people.name: Jawaharlal Nehru
important_people.description: First Prime Minister of independent India

current_conflicts: India faces ongoing border disputes with neighboring countries such as China and Pakistan, particularly in regions like Jammu & Kashmir and Arunachal Pradesh. Internal challenges include insurgencies and communal tensions in certain areas.
